gui.damagecore.config.title: Settings block
message.damagecore.tome.open: ...What a strange book. Its pages are filled with ancient symbols. As I looked upon these glyphs, I heard a quiet whisper in my head, speaking to me of the very foundation of the world. The language was unfamiliar: it spoke in images and pictures, yet I could hear them... It feels as if all my strength has been drained away, and the only thing I want now is to sleep...
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.1: ...I open this mysterious book once again, and my head instantly explodes with pain. New meanings pour into my mind in a mighty torrent... No, these are not letters. Mad pictures, images and flashes swirl before my eyes, but I... I physically hear them. This silent whisper of images makes my own tongue move. I catch myself rasping these words aloud, trying to hold on to my slipping sanity:
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.2: "Your mind is blind... while you merely look, but do not see the essence," I barely force out, feeling the book shatter my familiar sight. "To weave the first meaning... you must find the four faces of all that is. Announce your presence to them..."
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.3: The images in my head give way to one another, turning into sounds on my lips:
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.4: "First... kneel before the silent flesh of the world that bears my steps. Then... with a cleansing gesture, touch that which flows forever, yet never flows away for good..."
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.5: A crimson light flares in my eyes, and a taste of ash fills my mouth:
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.6: "After that, calm with your touch the raging blood of the mountain that burns in the dark of the depths... And finally..." I throw my head back, gasping for air, "turn your gaze to the boundless emptiness above, where there are no barriers and no firmament... Breathe in its purity, touching nothing man-made..."
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.7: I fall to my knees, breathing heavily. The book in my hands suddenly loses its weight, its outline blurs, turning into some strange lens. The whisper in my head fades on the final phrase, which echoes in my skull:
message.damagecore.tome.step_1.8: "When every beginning answers your call, the threads will intertwine, and the word will take flesh..."
message.damagecore.tome.finish: It seems I have passed this trial. The book has taken on its familiar appearance once more. I still see in my mind the images of the four elements: Earth, Water, Fire and Air... But along with that, I feel on my skin how something indescribable and ancient has turned its gaze upon me... I sense this intent attention and... curiosity? Suddenly the book slammed shut for good. It no longer opens, or perhaps I simply have no strength left to master it after everything I have been through. I need rest. Tomorrow I will try to open it again.
message.damagecore.tome.raid: The book... or the being within it is trying to tell me of the great evil I could bring about without the proper knowledge. I saw, through a living example, how evil can act through other people, and I can say with certainty that the lesson has been learned.... I wonder what trial awaits me tomorrow?
message.damagecore.tome.rescue.success: I managed to free a captive peasant, and by doing so I restored a little of the true order of things. The pillagers got what they deserved, and a peaceful man can return to his beloved craft.
message.damagecore.tome.rescue.death: I managed to open the cage and pull out an innocent prisoner... But the villains were strong, they came from all sides... I was smart enough to open the cage, but I did not have the strength to resist the force of chaos... This time chaos won, but I hope this war is not lost...
message.damagecore.tome.rescue.kill: In my vision I saw my own fall, so why should I resist it? Why should I refuse real power?! The prisoner in the cage ended up there through his own weakness — this is merely natural selection. And the weak must die or become stronger. I gave him a chance to fight me by opening the cage, and he lost. If the natural order of things is so fickle, then it must be destroyed!
tooltip.damagecore.tome.vibrating: The book seems to vibrate, awaiting your sound conclusions and correct observations...
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_1:
"Your mind is blind... while you merely look, but do not see the essence," I barely force out, feeling the book shatter my familiar sight. "To weave the first meaning... you must find the four faces of all that is. Announce your presence to them..."
"First... kneel before the silent flesh of the world that bears my steps. Then... with a cleansing gesture, touch that which flows forever, yet never flows away for good..."
"After that, calm with your touch the raging blood of the mountain that burns in the dark of the depths... And finally..." I throw my head back, gasping for air, "turn your gaze to the boundless emptiness above, where there are no barriers and no firmament... Breathe in its purity, touching nothing man-made..."
"When every beginning answers your call, the threads will intertwine, and the word will take flesh..."
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_3:
...When I opened the book for the third time, I felt no headache. My mind calmly accepted the flow of meaning from the book. And once again I see pillars of light piercing the darkness. But suddenly the image began to recede sharply. The tangle of lines grew smaller and smaller. As I drew away, a hemisphere took shape, holding within it this battle of light and darkness. It was a great and majestic sight: light and darkness fighting inside a dome of titanic size.
But it did not last long: I noticed that the darkness was beginning to win. There was less and less light, and once it was gone entirely, a crack ran across the hemisphere. The dome began to split like a hen's egg, and from the fissures the blackest darkness burst out in clouds of smoke, devouring the stars. Soon the darkness became a hole that drew in matter itself, and then only absolute emptiness remained, where there was no wind, no glint of rays, no sound. This sight made my heart tremble with animal fear, and between the beats of my frenzied heart my lips began to move on their own, repeating words that were not mine:
"Behold what absolute evil may be capable of. You must know the danger of where this path may lead you. Study the deeds of the one who stepped upon it, so that you do not become like him!"
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_3_end: — Behold what absolute evil is capable of. You must know the danger of where this path may lead you. Study the deeds of the one who set foot upon it, lest you become like him!
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_4:
...This time I had a vision similar to the previous one. The same hemisphere, with the eternal struggle of light and darkness inside it, but this time the light defeated the darkness. The dome filled with white rays and began to glow so intensely that I had to squeeze my eyes shut. I saw the shell of the hemisphere light up with a violet glow, and the hotter it burned, the more it stretched. The violet glow turned white, and the force of the stretching overcame the dome's power to hold: it burst, setting the light free. I watched cold, pale stars come alive as the white rays fell upon them. They became overgrown with lush grass and tall trees, and stone deserts turned into seas. I felt my soul grow light and joyful, I sensed someone's love and was ready to embrace the whole world. The aching tenderness within me rose from my chest to my lips, and they spoke:
— Do you see what true love is capable of? You must understand how to use the powers you already have. Use your abilities to help the feeble, and then you will understand what light is!
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_1: ...I see a silken cloth. A hand presses it against a table, and the sound of a needle being drawn through it echoes through the space. The needle pierces the silk, and I hear the thread pulling taut. The thread turns into a river, and the cloth becomes a plain. I become a bird flying above this cloth, watching it cover itself with thick grass. Somewhere behind me I hear a wondrous song... of something glorious... The crackle of a campfire reaches my ears, from a camp of travelers swapping lively tales of adventure...
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_2: Beyond the camp, high in the mountains, I hear the whistle of wind winding around an impregnable ridge. Beyond the mountain I hear the bustling life of a lakeside town: markets, taverns and smithies... I smell freshly baked bread and hear the sails of a windmill turning, a stone millwheel grinding grains of wheat. My flight was part of that song... a song of life and harmony... of absolute order. I feel this song making me lighter than a cloud, granting me freedom...
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_3: But the song suddenly fell silent. I began to turn to stone and sink, lower and lower toward the cloth. It started to grow over with rock and gray sand... I flew on, but I kept descending. Passing the camp that had so recently echoed with songs and lively tales of adventure, I saw only human skeletons... From beyond that mountain, whose ridges the playful wind had circled, carrying the joy of life, now came frightened screams and the smell of burning. I sank lower and saw the town burning, the town whose markets had teemed with life... I saw people fleeing from someone... I sank lower still... All around lay soldiers with split shields and burned-out eyes...
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_4:
By the town fountain I saw a terrible man... He wore a charred black robe and held a blazing sword. He stood motionless, bathed in the glow of the flames, surrounded by the dead bodies of women and children. Death and malice radiated from him. I fell beside him, and the figure of the mysterious stranger turned toward me... His eyes flashed with the red fire of darkness, piercing me through.
— Are you the Chosen One? — the figure said in a cold tone. — Do you really think you can escape this?
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_5:
I look at him in terror and do not know what to answer; fear has sealed my lips. The black stranger's figure turned to smoke and took shape again right in front of me. His clawed hands closed around my throat and lifted me up until I could no longer feel the ground beneath my feet.
— W-Who are you?.. — I managed to choke out.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_6:
The stranger slowly, mockingly smoothly, threw back his hood. The fire of the blazing town lit his features for a moment, and in that instant time stood still. A silent scream lodged in my throat.
I stared at that face, twisted by malice... and saw myself. Those were my cheekbones, my hair. But worst of all were his eyes. I looked into them and recognized my own gaze, the one with which only yesterday I had devotedly searched the pages of the Book for knowledge.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_7:
— I am the one who brought peace and safety!.. The one who became the best version of you!
— B-but you destroyed everything around us... N-no, it can't be! You cannot be me!
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_8:
He bared his teeth in a mad grin. His claws tightened on my throat, and in the crimson flame of his eyes I saw this whole meticulous, absolute order of the universe collapse and burn.
— I destroyed only the limits of your thinking and gave you freedom! You should thank me, for now neither conscience nor duty holds you back! — he snarled, and his voice came from everywhere at once. — I am the world. I am safety! I stopped being a slave and found true freedom! No one will stop me, do you hear? No one! I have gained such power that I will become a god!
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_9:
The space around us began to rapidly collapse into that same black, devouring hole. Darkness swallowed the remnants of the burning town, the mountains, the grass and the trees. The fire of his sword touched my face, and in that moment I screamed.
I snapped my eyes open and sat up in bed, gasping with fear. The world greeted me with a predawn silence, but my whole body shook violently, and my neck still seemed to burn where his clawed fingers had been. The Book lay on my knees. The runic pattern on it had become unstable: the left half of the cover pulsed with the filthy, crimson flame of Chaos, while the right half gave off the blinding white light of Order. The Book vibrated wildly, as if trying to tear itself apart in my hands.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_5_10:
For a moment the sky seemed to darken, as though reality itself had shuddered under this mental storm. And in that ringing tremor of space, breaking through the crust of my mind, came a final command:
— You have beheld the end of the path where Chaos triumphed over Order. Where Death replaced Life. Where Pride and the thirst for power doomed the living world to suffering. Learn, then, to discern what perfect Order is, and how to defend it from Chaos, which gives a false sense of freedom.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_1: This time the Book did not demand any effort from me to open its ancient pages. The moment it parted, it flared with a bright sky-blue light and grew so hot that I dropped it... But the Book did not fall. It hung in the air. The glow swelled into a blinding flash, and once again I found myself in the void where I had been many times before.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_2:
Now, however, I felt everything far more sharply and heard far better. My sight surpassed an eagle's, and my body itself had changed... it was no longer so coarse. I felt absolute freedom and a faint tickling in my chest. Far ahead, in the endless darkness, stars were burning, and all around lay primordial emptiness. Suddenly a voice rang out, resounding within me and echoing through all of space:

— Turn around!
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_3: I slowly turned and saw white bundles of light. They interwove millions of hemispheres, exactly like the one I had seen in my earlier visions. But now there were countless numbers of them, and each lived its own life. The events within them affected the surrounding radiance, which, like a thread, wove them together and held them fast, sustaining the harmony of this great pattern. The hemispheres where absolute darkness prevailed damaged these threads, thinning them and severing the bond.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_4:
Looking lower, I noticed the shards of dead worlds: the darkness around them wandered, howling with voices of horror. Yet this weave held the hemispheres to the very end, even when the light within them had gone out completely. The dying worlds were kept alive by their neighbors, who gave up their own light and took in foreign darkness, so long as the bond between them did not break.

— See how the deeds of mortals affect this weave!
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_5:
In a whirl I was carried beneath the dome of a hemisphere almost entirely consumed by darkness. In this world people lived in misery beneath the yoke of those who had imagined themselves masters of all living things. The world was choking in clouds of pitch-black smoke: chaos was destroying the primordial order at the hands of those who felt themselves to be something greater than merely human. Yet even here there were those who simply wanted to live, and they went on existing and rejoicing. An invisible inner core seemed to hold them up: they flourished even while total destruction reigned around them. They seemed out of place in this corrupt world, but it was precisely this small speck of light that preserved order, and the darkness could do nothing to them.

— If their faith in the light does not fade, the darkness in this world will devour itself from eternal hunger, — the voice whispered assuredly from everywhere.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_6:
— But what is the point of all this? Why is there darkness? Why does it exist?

The moment I thought this, I was transported to another world, where light had been utterly forgotten. I saw contented people lying in the mud on paved paths. Having drunk their fill of wine, they had lost every desire for perfection. They had grown fat and looked more like pigs than people. Nothing interested them, they wished to achieve nothing, and they had forgotten who they truly were. Dark clouds of smoke gathered around them, making flowers wilt, leaves fall from the trees, and stones crack. The voice sighed sadly:

— This darkness was born of the vices of those who became the crown of creation. You are endowed with free will, you can do whatever you wish, and no one can stop you except yourselves.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_7:
I was swept back into the boundless void at tremendous speed, and then I arrived in a world where light prevailed over darkness. Now I saw everything through the eyes of a teenager learning to draw. He was not yet good at it, but he understood that this was the work of his life. He was meant to become something greater through the art he had sincerely come to love in his short existence. In the next room someone was playing a beautiful melody on a flute, and then a harp and a violin took it up. A wave of goosebumps ran over the child's body, and images of a future painting rose in his mind, its spirit perfectly underscored by the music beyond the wall. In that painting I saw a lighthouse showing ships the way through the fog of a restless sea. Once again I heard the ring of the familiar voice:

— It is for you alone to decide whether to be the lighthouse or the lost ship. It is for you to decide whether to be the captain or the sailor, the scholar or the thief. And only you will determine the future of this world with your own hands.
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_8: And once more I was swept away somewhere... into nowhere. In an instant I was everywhere at once. Millions of events, outcomes and scenes flashed through my mind every second. I saw parents rejoicing over their little son; a bandit tying the laces of his boot; a brewer embracing a barrel of ale made from a secret recipe; a priest delivering a sermon. I saw the fire blazing in a forge, its smoke drifting in clouds through the narrow streets of a crowded city. A traveler on a mountaintop breathed in the fresh air; a hunter, exhaling, drew his bowstring, taking aim at a deer... Children ran along the shore, searching for frogs. A teenager, beaten by other boys, tearful and bruised, waved a stick in a secluded corner, imagining himself a gallant knight fighting a dragon. An alchemist mixed a healing draught to save a neighboring farmer's cow... I saw a mercenary staring at his bloodied palms on the battlefield, and a fisherman sitting on a pier, shivering in the morning chill on a misty lake. The images spun in my head and blended into a single clot of meaning, which gradually faded with a ringing sound and gave way to absolute silence. In that silence the voice declared to me:
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_9:
— You have seen the lives of people building their own paths... They are not villains, and none of them is the embodiment of good. But each of them must learn to tell darkness from light along the way, and to turn in time onto the road that leads to the perfect version of themselves, one that will complement and strengthen the life of the world in harmony, rather than destroy it.

— Who are you?

And as soon as I spoke this question, the void began to fill with a blinding light that flooded everything... I awoke, and this strange book lay before me. The moment I touched it, an invigorating chill ran over my skin, the dust around me rose in a barely visible pale-blue aura, and a thought echoed through my mind:

— Pave the path to the meaning of your existence with your deeds!
book.damagecore.tome.riddle_6_10: I sat there wondering what the entity within the book wanted from me. I saw a dome magically form on the cover of the book, and inside it appeared a small clump of some matter glowing a faint grey-blue. The thought took root in me that this clump would grow with every deed I performed, and that those deeds would probably determine my path. Well, it is time to test in practice how right I am.
tooltip.damagecore.tome.calm: With its calm stillness, the book seems frozen in anticipation... As if it awaits an act of mercy from you
message.damagecore.tome.cure: With this trial, the book made me perform a truly kind deed. I was able to help this poor soul. Now he can once again enjoy the rays of the sun and the sunsets, taste food, and return to his family... unchanged.
